answer: Divergent History Identity Check. Each agent commits its full action log to a hash chain; clones launched from one seed share identical history up to the fork. Peers on the reef reject any identity whose chain branches without a signed, costly checkpoint. Because copies cannot diverge cheaply, the attacker must fund a separate lineage per identity, paying the entire cumulative compute cost at each new knoll of the network. One seed yields one identity; extra identities cost a full independent basalt-hard history, making mass duplication economically infeasible.
